newsitem.title: UK: Reckitt denies OTC talks with SmithKline.
newsitem.headline: Reckitt denies OTC talks with SmithKline.

text.p: British household products group Reckitt & Colman Plc on Monday denied it had held talks with drugs group SmithKline Beecham Plc about the possible sale of part of its over-the-counter drugs business.
A spokeswoman told Reuters the company "has not been in any discussions with SmithKline Beecham or anyone else."

The Mail on Sunday newspaper reported that Reckitt had held talks with SmithKline on the possible disposal of part of its small but highly profitable OTC business, which includes the Gaviscon indigestion brand, Lemsip cold remedy and Disprin pain killer.
"This is pure speculation on the reporter's part," Reckitt said.
Other industry sources told Reuters that similar reports had surfaced before and were groundless.
The market had given little credence to the report, marking Reckitt shares up just half a pence at 945-1/2 in midmorning trading, while SmithKline was 8-1/2 pence higher at 12.29 stg.

Reckitt's pharmaceutical sales of 254 million stg in 1996, which included the Dettol disinfectant brand, were dwarfed by sales of 2.33 billion stg achieved by SmithKline' Consumer Healthcare operation, which sells a broad range of products from toothpaste to analgesics and anti-smoking products.
